newsitem.title: KENYA: Top developments on Monday in Zaire crisis.
newsitem.headline: Top developments on Monday in Zaire crisis.

text.p: Following are the top developments on Monday in the crisis in eastern Zaire.

--Laurent Kabila, leader of rebel forces in eastern Zaire, said he was calling a three-week unilateral ceasefire from 5 p.m. (1500 GMT) on Monday to allow Rwandan refugees to leave for home. He said combat would resume if Zairean troops failed to respect the rebel ceasefire.
--In Kigali, an Organisation of African Unity peace mission opened talks aimed at securing a ceasefire in eastern Zaire and return home 1.1 million trapped Rwandan refugees.
--In Geneva, the U.N. refugee agency chief, Sadako Ogata, called for international efforts to create protected humanitarian corridors in Zaire to coax Rwandan refugees back into their homeland.
--In Kinshasa, Zaire said it would not attend regional talks on the crisis scheduled on Tuesday in Nairobi.
--In Paris, France urged the United States, Europe and Africa into urgent talks on how to restore security in eastern Zaire and help avert disaster for the refugees.
